content.title: TV Dispute Has Fans Scrambling To Watch The Masters Saturday
content.text: Key PointsComcast-CBS dispute prevents subscribers from watching the Masters on TV, offering access via Paramount Plus.Fans express frustration over rising costs, app fragmentation, and sports viewing becoming inconvenient.Suggested workarounds include using TV antennas, the Masters app, and opposing broadcast TV mergers. Stop us if you’ve heard this one before: Fans have woken up to find that they can’t watch a major sporting event due to a TV dispute. A number of Comcast subscribers woke up on Saturday expecting to watch the third round of the Masters, only to find that a dispute between CBS and the cable company is keeping the Masters off the air. According to reports, it is currently only available to them via the Paramount Plus app. “You’ve got to be kidding me that CBS and Comcast are in a dispute in Nashville and the Masters isn’t on. What are we doing here, guys, it’s a free channel! These channel disputes are out of control. Sports fans are getting screwed everywhere,” longtime broadcaster Clay Travis wrote on X. “Hey @comcast get it together. Not being able to watch the Masters is (expletive) . @Verizon you up?” another user on X wrote. “I pay a fee for my home internet @comcast , I pay a fee for Prime @amazon , I’m watching the Masters with commercials! Homemade pimento sandwich cost more than I could buy one at the tournament! Soon I will be priced out of watching #themasters,” a third remarked. The Solutions For many fans, there are a number of workarounds to this issue in general. Antenna TV, the Masters app and a general opposition to broadcast TV mergers are all short- and long-term solutions. “Download the free masters app and within the app you can mirror the broadcast to your TV,” one user suggested on X. “Well then you should be strongly against broadcast TV mergers that increase retransmission leverage,” another wrote. “You’re not so young, Clay that you’ve never had a tv antenna, are you? It’s a free channel indeed,” wrote a third. Apr 8, 2026; Augusta, Georgia, USA; Wyndham Clark and his girlfriend Alicia Bogdanski stands with the pin flag on the second hole during the Par 3 Contest at the Masters Tournament at Augusta National Golf Club. Mandatory Credit: Katie Goodale-Imagn Images© Katie Goodale-Imagn Images. “Horrible news I can’t watch the Masters. Good news is I’ll never watch cbs Nash again. Ever.” “I’m 60yrs old and starting to find something else to do. Some of it’s about money but mostly it’s about sports being scattered on all different apps. Go hiking, swimming, motorcycle riding etc young people.” “Hopefully this is the tip of the iceberg. I can’t watch my red wings or Tigers without paying 20 bucks a month. Have to get Amazon to watch certain things as well. It’s ridiculous. Take me back to 1995 cable TV.” Sports fans seem to rapidly be approaching the “scoff price” of watching sports in general. The more the companies try to gouge consumers for every dollar for the privilege of watching their favorite sporting events, the more it will turn them away towards something less expensive.
